title: feat: show top-up links when text balance is too low
author: voodoohop
pr_body_excerpt:
- Adds an unbilled low-balance notice with top-up and quest links for text output, including streaming. Explains whom to contact when the account belongs to an app or service owner.
- Keeps JSON modes, audio/media output and API-key budget failures on HTTP 402. Notices are never cached or billed and remain 402 failures in analytics.
- Counts anonymous arrivals from each link in Tinybird; no unique-user or purchase attribution.
- Controls the feature with `TEXT_BALANCE_NOTICE_ENABLED` in `gen.pollinations.ai/src/middleware/text-balance-notice.ts`, currently `true`. Set it to `false` and deploy through the normal pipeline to restore HTTP 402. No Cloudflare binding is required.
- Independent adversarial and Claude Fable reviews completed; verified HEAD and audio issues fixed. The Flagship experiment remains in commits `650d63ab69` and `f11186a5ca`, followed by an explicit revert that restores the previously tested implementation.

gist.headline: A gentler empty jar
gist.blurb: When text balance runs low, the hive now leaves a useful little signpost instead of a bare 402 wall. Top up, try a Quest, or find the person holding the app’s wallet.
gist.summary: Text requests with insufficient unbilled balance now return a low-balance notice with Top Up and Quest links, including streaming responses, while JSON modes, audio/media output, and API-key budget failures keep their HTTP 402 behavior.
gist.impact: People arriving through an app or service get a clear path to add Pollen, earn it through Quests, or contact the account owner, without notices being cached or billed.
gist.visual_concept: A cozy text-generation garden has a nearly empty Pollen jar beside a retro terminal, but a friendly signpost offers two paths: Top Up and Quests. Polli, wearing a tiny gardener tool belt, points warmly toward the paths while code-flowers continue growing; this represents a helpful low-balance response rather than a blocked, sterile error page.
